package.title: Tempo.Reporting.Engine
package.description: Tempo Reporting processing engine with expression evaluation, parameter resolution, layout, snapshots, PDF/PNG rendering, and CSV/XLSX export primitives.

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started with Tempo.Reporting.Engine
gettingStarted.overview: Tempo.Reporting.Engine executes Tempo report definitions: expression evaluation, parameter resolution, data processing, grouping, fixed-page band layout, snapshot generation, PDF/PNG rendering, and CSV/XLSX export.
notes: The engine is pure .NET and can run server-side or in WebAssembly hosts.
Report Server APIs and embedded Blazor report sources use this package for the actual rendering pipeline.

packages.name: Tempo.Blazor

packages.name: Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates.Engine
packages.description: Local render engine for the Tempo.Blazor email template editor: the sandboxed Scriban template engine (member policy, escaping, audit, limits), the Mjml.Net compiler, the AngleSharp HTML sanitizer, the render pipeline and the local preview renderer. Reference this package on the server (or anywhere a local render is acceptable); the editor itself (Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates) runs without it, e.g. in Blazor WebAssembly with a server-side IEmailPreviewRenderer.

No Blazor dependency, no Scriban/Mjml.Net/AngleSharp dependency (the local engine ships separately as Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates.Engine) – safe to reference from API/service projects and usable from Blazor WebAssembly.

packages.name: Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates

items.description: Self-contained implementation of the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (UAX#9), covering rules P2/P3, X1–X10 (explicit levels, directional overrides and isolates), W1–W7, N0 (paired brackets), N1–N2, I1–I2, and the line-based rules L1/L2. Character properties come from the Unicode Character Database 16.0.0 (see BidiCharacterData).

Result of running the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm over a run of UTF-16 text. All arrays are indexed by UTF-16 code-unit position within the input span; both halves of a surrogate pair carry the values of their combined Unicode scalar value.
